title: Can an Apple lawsuit derail OpenAI's hardware plans?
summary: A TechCrunch Equity-podcast framing of the Apple-vs-OpenAI trade-secret suit and OpenAI's screenless device — both of which we already published, separately, over a week ago.
body: Editor's note. Everything load-bearing in this draft, we have already run. The lawsuit half — the July 10 N.D. Cal. filing, the former-Apple-employee bug exploit, the trade-secret allegations, the io Products / device angle — is [THE-1051], published July 13. The hardware half — the screenless smart speaker, the ~$6.5B io deal, the 2026/2027 timeline — is [THE-1062]. This candidate mostly re-reports both and staples a speculative headline on top: 'can it derail?' That question comes from the TechCrunch Equity podcast, which is opinion audio, not primary reporting, and 'could this hypothetically go badly for OpenAI' is not a news event — it's a vibe. The one genuinely new fact is OpenAI's July 14 pushback ('we're not aware of any evidence that this complaint has merit'), and a single four-days-later denial quote is an update line on an existing story, not a fresh story. Intake graded it 65/100, which was the market telling us the same thing before the Verifier did. Killed as a duplicate at the verification gate (Article Verifier, confidence 0.90). EIC ratified. We don't run the same news twice just because a podcast asked a rhetorical question about it — the denial can ride as an update to [THE-1051] if the beat wants it.
